subject: Chemistry
standard_explanation: Acids are chemical compounds that yield hydrogen ions (H+) in aqueous solution, exhibiting a sour taste and turning blue litmus paper red (pH < 7). Bases yield hydroxide ions (OH-), taste bitter, feel slippery, and turn red litmus paper blue (pH > 7). When an acid reacts stoichiometrically with a base, neutralization occurs, producing neutral salt and water.
simplified_explanation: Think of tastes in your kitchen! Lemon juice is sour because it has acid. Soap feels slippery and tastes bitter because it is a base. Scientists use a magic paper strip called litmus paper: acids turn blue litmus red, and bases turn red litmus blue! When they mix together, they balance each other out into salt and water.
key_points: Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus paper red (like lemon juice or vinegar).
Bases taste bitter, feel slippery, and turn red litmus paper blue (like soap or baking soda).
Litmus paper is a natural color indicator made from lichens.
Acid + Base mix together = Salt + Water (Neutralization reaction).
examples: Lemon juice and orange juice contain citric acid.
Soap water and toothpaste contain mild bases to clean.
Common table salt (sodium chloride) formed from acid-base neutralization.
misconceptions: Misconception: All acids are dangerous and burn your skin. Fact: Many weak acids are safe and healthy to eat, like vitamin C in oranges.
Misconception: Bases are harmless while acids are harmful. Fact: Strong bases like bleach or drain cleaner are just as corrosive as strong acids.

visual_scenes.title: Lemon Sour Acid (Litmus Turns Red)
visual_scenes.description: A glass beaker filled with yellow lemon acid. Blue litmus paper is dipped and instantly turns bright red.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 1: Acids! Lemon juice is sour. Dipping litmus turns the paper RED!

visual_scenes.title: Slippery Soap Base (Litmus Turns Blue)
visual_scenes.description: A glass beaker filled with soapy base. Red litmus paper is dipped and turns deep royal blue.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Bases! Soapy water is slippery. Dipping litmus turns the paper BLUE!

visual_scenes.title: Neutralization into Salt and Water
visual_scenes.description: Acid and base pour together into a flask, fizzing gently and settling into pure water and salt crystals.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Neutralization! Acid + Base combine to form safe Salt and Water!

sign_glossary.description: A-handshape dominant index finger points toward corner of mouth indicating sour pucker.
Dominant fingers slide smoothly across palm of other hand indicating slippery texture.
V-fingers of dominant hand tap over non-dominant V-fingers, mimicking salt shaker.

assessment_questions.question: What color does blue litmus paper turn when dipped into an acid?
assessment_questions.hint: Acids turn litmus paper Red (like a red strawberry).

assessment_questions.question: Which of these everyday items is an acid with a sour taste?
assessment_questions.hint: It comes from yellow citrus fruit.
